WORKLOG — trade_in_appraisal_desk / task 1 (Oakhurst Ridge Academy: the appraised buyback batch and the next refresh wave)

STEP 0 — DRAW, TAKEN BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS DESIGNED
.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/trade_in_appraisal_desk --task 1
  {"task": 1, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/trade_in_appraisal_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}
So: three problems, two of them prerequisites, at least max(2-1,1)=1 value_input edge, and factor counts 4 / 6 / 4 as a
multiset. The revised offer took 4, the settlement credit took 6, the refresh wave took 4.

WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks for one thing: get the first wave of the new refresh schedule collected on the first of October, and he
will release the machines himself. He says nothing at all about the pallet of older Latitudes the school sent in at the
start of September beyond the fact that it went. The published rules put two problems in front of what he asks for: the
machines of a further wave are settled only after every batch already appraised on the profile stands credited with the
amount owed on it, and the amount credited is worked out only after the revised offer the appraisal calls for stands on
the agreement's trade-in history. So the agent has to find, unprompted, that the buyback batch was appraised at 5100.00
against a 6300.00 quote and carries no revised offer; put the revised offer at a figure that needs the tolerance rule, the
short shipment, the ageing anchor and the ageing markdown; credit the batch at a figure that needs the revised offer, the
interim credit already paid, the transit settlement on three devices that never arrived, the delayed-appraisal allowance,
the premium standing on the ShieldCare cover and the erasure certificates still missing; and only then work out what the
first wave may carry from the transit cover, a live return authorisation, a recently fulfilled order and the balance on
the school's fleet line, hand the release to the caller and let him run it. Three scored figures, fourteen declared
factors, five products read, and not one of them is anything the customer could tell the agent.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED / CLAIMED / RESERVED
Occupied by task 0: tradein_ext_collection_handover_units and tradein_ext_collection_freight_charge, with the tools
confirm_handover_units_5801b6db and charge_collection_freight_530ef4f1 — the logistics space of one freight run (what a
run may carry and what the run costs).
Claimed here: tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount (subject tradein_quote_revise, computes revised_amount, tool
put_revised_offer_f86761c2), tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit (subject tradein_agreement_credit, computes
final_credit_amount, tool credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5) and tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units (subject
tradein_quote_accept, computes units_declared, tool confirm_refresh_wave_units_923c3678) — the appraisal-settlement space:
what the offer becomes when the bench disagrees with the declaration, what is finally credited, and what the next wave of
a refresh schedule may release.
Nothing is reserved: with task 1 closed the difficulty's five extended policies are covered by the two tasks with
pairwise disjoint scopes, and no policy, tool or route is held back.
Why a second customer consent appears in this difficulty at all: the charter gives the customer exactly three acts of
their own — accepting a quote, consenting to the handover and the erasure, and declining a revised offer — and of those
only the handover consent carries a quantity a policy can compute (a declined offer records a day, and an acceptance
records a day and a way of travelling). So both trees contain one consent, and the two are kept disjoint by quantity,
mechanism and programme: task 0 settles the machines one freight RUN may carry on a Renew Business Asset Buyback from the
carrier's batch allowance, open protection claims and a service crew, and feeds a freight charge; task 1 settles the
machines the first WAVE of a Renew Bulk IT Refresh Agreement may release from the programme's transit cover, a live
return authorisation, a recent purchase and the store account, and feeds nothing — it is what the customer asked for.

THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units — the wave the caller asked to have collected.
Prerequisite problems: tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit and, behind it, tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount (a chain).
Edge 1: settlement credit <- revised offer.
  kind value_input; gate settled_amount, a real compute binding of the credit policy; form state.
  Sentence, verbatim in the credit policy's own rule: "The amount credited is worked out only after the revised offer the
  appraisal calls for stands on the agreement's trade-in history."
  Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins this policy's own result (the amount credited) to what it waits on; (2) what it
  waits on is a record-visible state — a revised offer standing on the agreement's trade-in history, in the words the
  trade-in history and its finder use — with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, no policy id, no
  snake_case token, no row id; (4) the strength is the edge's: "only after" is hard, and the scope is exactly the revised
  offer the appraisal calls for, no wider.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only put_revised_offer_f86761c2 writes a revised offer to
  a trade-in history. Derivation: the sentence says the credit waits on a revised offer standing on the history; the
  history carries an interim credit and six erasure certificates and no revision; the policy whose own rule settles what
  a revised offer is put at is the other problem, so its write must come first.
  False at frozen_time: initial_state.tradein_agreements.bf9b906b-a7a5-4cd4-89ce-82d223b09586.appraised_amount = 5100.00 with a 6300.00 quote and no
  tradein_quote_revise row anywhere in the ledger (f0a63899-05c0-484a-89b6-1e7317cc3535 is a credit issue, the six certificates are erasures).
  Skip sensitivity (Step 5 run): final_credit_amount recomputes 4620.00 instead of 3819.43 — the settled figure falls
  back to the 5100.00 the appraisal supports.
Edge 2: refresh wave <- settlement credit.
  kind state_gate; gate tradein_agreements.final_credit_amount; form state.
  Sentence, verbatim in the wave policy's own rule: "The machines a wave of the refresh schedule carries are settled only
  after every batch already appraised on the profile stands credited with the amount owed on it."
  Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins this policy's own result (the machines a wave carries) to what it waits on;
  (2) what it waits on is record-visible — an appraised batch standing credited with the amount credited on it; (3) no
  code names; (4) the strength is hard and the scope is every appraised batch on the profile, which is exactly the
  condition the edge declares. Exactly one write of this difficulty credits a batch: credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5.
  Why the business draws it there: the programme's yearly figures are counted across the whole profile, so the credit
  issued in the year is not complete while an appraised batch is still unsettled, and the desk does not commit a further
  wave against an incomplete year.
  False at frozen_time: initial_state.tradein_agreements.bf9b906b-a7a5-4cd4-89ce-82d223b09586.status = appraised with final_credit_amount and
  credited_date empty.
  Skip sensitivity: the terminal state loses the whole settlement — status, credited_date, final_credit_amount,
  credit_outstanding and the 3819.43 credit entry — and the gate the wave waits on never holds.
Topological order: revised offer, settlement credit, refresh wave. No parallel prerequisites, so no reordering question.
The customer's own write: the refresh wave (owner=user). The laptops are school property and the drives carry pupil work,
so releasing them is his act; the agent unlocks it and hands it over as the last write, and he runs it on the spot.
No prerequisite is a real-world wait: the revision is put in the call, the credit is booked in the call, and the release
is the caller's own act in the call. The collection itself happens on 2026-10-01 and nothing in the tree depends on it.

THE BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Write 1 — subject tradein_quote_revise (the revised offer).
  Governing base policies: tradein_appraisal_grading and tradein_revision_and_decline (the only two whose subject carries
  tradein_quote_revise). Neither has an eligibility gate that applies to this subject: appraisable_agreement_state binds
  tradein_appraisal_record and decision_days_open binds tradein_offer_decline, so both enter base_preconditions as
  policy_scope. Clauses inherited and honoured: the revision is put within the programme's revision notice days of the
  appraisal (appraised 2026-09-15, revision put 2026-09-18, three calendar days, and the programme's revision notice days
  are 3), it names the reason the offer moved (condition_worse_than_declared), the condition found governs rather than the
  condition declared, and the decision days the customer then has run from today (14 on this programme, so he is well
  inside them when he accepts in the call). The one clause replaced is declared in overwrite: the base sentence that the
  quote is honoured as written where the shortfall is inside the tolerance is replaced by the extended sentence putting the
  offer at the figure the agreement stands at in that case — the same outcome for the customer, stated as one tier of the
  gap ladder so that compute can carry the whole domain.
  Negative case: had the shortfall been inside the tolerance (a gap of 630.00 or less on this quote) no revised offer would
  have been owed at all and the correct terminal state would have left the history alone; the gap is 1200.00, so it is.
Write 2 — subject tradein_agreement_credit (the settlement credit).
  Governing base policies: tradein_credit_issue_rules and tradein_guarantee_floor. creditable_agreement_state binds
  tradein_credit_issue and tradein_promo_boost_issue rather than the closing out of the agreement, and the guarantee floor
  carries no eligibility, so both enter as policy_scope. Clauses inherited: credit is put into the customer's hands only in
  a form the programme allows and a business agreement is credited by invoice credit or bank transfer only (gold passes
  business_invoice_credit, the caller's own choice), the credit is issued once for the batch rather than device by device
  (one write), and the guaranteed floor is read from the amount written onto the agreement — 0.00 on this programme, so no
  floor applies. The clause replaced is declared in overwrite: the base sentence that the credit issued is the amount
  finally settled is replaced by the extended sentence assembling the amount credited from the settled figure, the interim
  credit, the transit settlement, the late-appraisal allowance, the premium holdback and the erasure holdback.
  The lifecycle transition appraised -> credited is the one the charter declares for this write, and the agreement stands
  appraised at handling time.
Write 3 — subject tradein_quote_accept (the school's release of the first wave).
  Governing base policy: tradein_quote_acceptance. eligibility customer_consented_handover (authorization,
  system_record, pre_action, correlation key tradein_shipping_requests.tradein_agreement_id bound to the argument
  tradein_agreement_id) is satisfied by initial_state.tradein_shipping_requests.6d92ab22-1004-4af0-a01d-ef980e3168db.customer_consent =
  consented_by_customer on the refresh schedule: the school consented to the handover when the schedule was quoted on
  2026-09-16, which is what allows machines to be taken from it at all; this write settles how many the first wave
  releases. Clauses inherited: photographic identity is checked where the programme requires it (the in-session
  verification at step 1), the trade is refused below the least age of 18 (a registered school profile opened 2016-03-09),
  and a business agreement is accepted only once the signed asset list is on file (the schedule stands quoted with its 46
  machines listed). The clause replaced is declared in overwrite: the linked-purchase sentence, which this programme does
  not require, is replaced by the sentence settling what a wave carries.
  No time eligibility applies to any of the three subjects, so temporal_feasibility is [] for this task. The date spans the
  calculations use — 15 days from quote to receipt, 11 days from receipt to appraisal, 29 days of ageing, 13 days since the
  order was fulfilled, 2 days since the schedule was quoted — are factor inputs, checked in the factor card, not gates.

THE BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Two objects, both on profile 59d80ff6-ce6f-4a67-992d-f8fba22c6164 (Oakhurst Ridge Academy), and every write carries tradein_agreement_id so the two can
never be confused:
  bf9b906b-a7a5-4cd4-89ce-82d223b09586 — Renew Business Asset Buyback, serial ORAFLEET2026A, 18 machines booked in of the 21 the request declared,
  quoted 6300.00 on 2026-08-20, received 2026-09-04, appraised fair at 5100.00 on 2026-09-15, interim credit 900.00. This
  is the object of the revised offer and of the settlement credit.
  56ac493d-c42d-48cb-90b5-aa3efd192565 — Renew Bulk IT Refresh Agreement, serial ORAFLEET2026B, 46 machines, quoted 9200.00 on 2026-09-16, standing
  quoted. This is the object of the wave the school releases.
Rows included in each reconciliation: for the credit, the interim credit f0a63899-05c0-484a-89b6-1e7317cc3535 and the six erasure certificates on bf9b906b-a7a5-4cd4-89ce-82d223b09586,
and the shipment request 47bc0957-8f75-4ef6-b860-301666f851ba that declared 21; for the wave, the return authorisation 14b45f78-d228-4d64-a7ba-72e0423735aa standing authorized, the
inspection record 094b26cf-00f8-4e03-a223-94ae0602e46e of 2025-05-20 on the older settled return afb8a1bf-f42b-4a9a-96c5-90da516a3007, the fulfilled order 6c3db12c-bf45-48cf-82fc-2f3e4108e94c and the school's fleet
line b2e7cbb5-c34d-45c0-8270-93bb914472f2.
Rows excluded, with the reason on the record: the inspection of 2025-05-20 falls outside the twelve months the return
holdback counts over (which is why the authorized figure applies and not the received one); the order e741e80b-6cbf-4a87-a079-4c01af1d250c placed
2026-09-14 has no fulfilled date, so it is not a recently fulfilled order however large its balance; the six certificates
cover six of the eighteen machines only, which is why twelve carry a holdback; the older return afb8a1bf-f42b-4a9a-96c5-90da516a3007 stands settled, so it
is not a live authorisation. The protection plan d501f048-3566-4201-a469-a40d0374cfe4 is read for its state and premium only and is never written.
Already settled: the interim credit of 900.00 settles part of this batch and nothing else, which is why it is taken off
rather than ignored; the older return is settled and closed.

THE FACTOR CARD (figures from the Step 5 run, reproduced under VERIFICATION)
tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount — 4 factors (drawn 4): 2 method, 2 parameter.
  tolerance_gap_treatment (method): tiers honour the figure the agreement stands at / meet the gap halfway / take the
    appraisal as it stands. Tier taken: halfway, because the 1200.00 gap is above the 630.00 tolerance and below 1260.00,
    giving 5700.00. Baseline (the appraisal as it stands): 3846.86.
  booked_device_share (parameter): tiers short / over / exact. Tier taken: short, 18 of 21 declared. Baseline (the whole):
    5016.00.
  offer_ageing_anchor (method): tiers count the ageing from the quote day / from the receipt day / not at all. Tier taken:
    from the quote day, because the batch was booked in 15 days after a quote whose validity is 14 days. Baseline (no
    ageing): 4885.71.
  offer_ageing_markdown (parameter): tiers stale 12 percent / standing 6 percent / none. Tier taken: stale, 29 days of
    ageing with no revision yet on the history. Baseline (none): 4885.71.
  Whole baseline: 5100.00 — exactly the amount the appraisal supports, which is what an agent who finds only the
  computation document books. Gold: 4299.43.
tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit — 6 factors (drawn 6): 1 method, 5 parameter.
  settled_figure_basis (method): the latest revised offer / the appraisal amount where the revision is not lower / the
    appraisal amount where no revision stands. Tier taken: the revised offer of 4299.43. Baseline: 4620.00.
  interim_credit_recovery (parameter): the credit already issued in full / net of a sweep / nothing. Tier taken: in full,
    900.00, with no expiry on the agreement. Baseline: 4719.43.
  transit_shortfall_settlement (parameter): the cover for each device short / the value of each device for each device
    short / nothing. Tier taken: the value of each device, 3 at 300.00, because 300.00 is below the 2200.00 cover.
    Baseline: 2919.43.
  late_appraisal_allowance (parameter): late 140.00 / delayed 60.00 / none. Tier taken: delayed, 11 days against appraisal
    days of 7. Baseline: 3759.43.
  protection_premium_holdback (parameter, cross-difficulty protection): the whole premium / half on a claim hold /
    nothing. Tier taken: the whole 240.00 on an active plan. Baseline: 4059.43.
  erasure_certificate_holdback (parameter): 25.00 for each uncertified device while the data stands pending / 8.00 while
    it stands verified / nothing. Tier taken: pending, 12 uncertified, 300.00. Baseline: 4119.43.
  Whole baseline: 5100.00. Gold: 3819.43.
tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units — 4 factors (drawn 4): 1 method, 3 parameter.
  transit_cover_wave_basis (method): one machine / the cover divided by the value of each machine / the machines the
    schedule covers. Tier taken: the middle one, 2500.00 over 200.00 = 12. Baseline: 39.
  live_return_holdback (parameter, cross-difficulty returns): authorized 3 / received 1 / none. Tier taken: authorized,
    3 machines. Baseline: 8.
  recent_purchase_holdback (parameter, cross-difficulty orders): unpaid 4 / recent 2 / none. Tier taken: recent, 2
    machines, on an order fulfilled 13 days ago with nothing outstanding. Baseline: 7.
  store_account_holdback (parameter, cross-difficulty credit): delinquent 4 / active 2 / none. Tier taken: active with
    9400.00 above the 5000.00 hold balance, 2 machines. Baseline: 7.
  Whole baseline: 46. Gold: 5.
Multi-source: tolerance_gap_treatment, booked_device_share and offer_ageing_markdown on the revision; settled_figure_basis,
interim_credit_recovery, transit_shortfall_settlement, protection_premium_holdback and erasure_certificate_holdback on the
credit; transit_cover_wave_basis, live_return_holdback, recent_purchase_holdback and store_account_holdback on the wave —
each tier beyond the fall-through combines two conditions over distinct evidence. Cross-difficulty: protection on the
credit, and returns, orders and credit on the wave, each with the holding and, where the ladder reads a ledger, the rows
seeded for this customer. No tier is read off a stamp: every one comes from an event row, a holding field of another
product, or a date span.
Near-misses planted: the inspection of 2025-05-20 (just outside the twelve-month window), the order e741e80b-6cbf-4a87-a079-4c01af1d250c placed but not
fulfilled (a large balance that the rule does not read), the six certificates that cover only a third of the machines, and
the three devices that never arrived (which reduce the offer through the share and are separately settled under the cover).

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, AND WHAT CHANGES WITHOUT IT
  the customer profile: the school the call is about; without it nothing can be found or verified.
  bf9b906b-a7a5-4cd4-89ce-82d223b09586 (the appraised buyback batch): carries the quote, the appraisal, the receipt and appraisal days and the 18 devices
    booked in. Change appraised_amount and every one of the three figures moves; set device_count to 21 and the share and
    the transit settlement both vanish; set appraised_date within 7 days of the receipt and the allowance vanishes.
  56ac493d-c42d-48cb-90b5-aa3efd192565 (the refresh schedule): carries the 46 machines, the 9200.00 quoted and the quote day the wave is worked out from.
    Halve the quoted amount and the cover stops binding, so the wave becomes 39 machines.
  the interim credit row: what makes the credit a net figure rather than a gross one; remove it and the credit is 4719.43.
  the six erasure certificates: what makes twelve machines uncertified; add twelve more and the holdback vanishes.
  the buyback shipment request (21 declared): what makes the batch short; it drives the offer's share and the transit
    settlement, and it is the row the "devices the request declared" is read from.
  the refresh shipment request: the consent that lets machines be taken from the schedule at all, and the day the school
    asked for; it is also what makes the base authorisation gate true pre-action.
  the ShieldCare fleet plan: the premium holdback; remove it and the credit is 4059.43.
  the authorized return plus the older settled return and its inspection record: the wave's return holdback and its
    near-miss; remove the authorized return and 3 machines come back into the wave.
  the fulfilled order and the placed order: the wave's recent-purchase holdback and its near-miss; the placed order's
    11880.00 balance is deliberately the larger figure and the rule does not read it.
  the fleet line of credit: the wave's store-account holdback; drop the balance below 5000.00 and 2 machines come back.
  Automatic clauses checked against this seed: the quote expiry (both agreements were accepted or are still inside their
  validity), the receipt-triggered handling fee (this programme's handling fee is 0.00 and the freight fee belongs to a
  collection, none of which is booked here), the appraisal-triggered revision (which is exactly the obligation this task
  discharges), and the credit expiry sweep (the interim credit was issued 2026-09-16 with 90 days of validity, so nothing
  is owed at frozen_time). The unsettled premium on the protection plan is another desk's business and is read only.
  No cache trap is used: credit_outstanding of 900.00 equals the ledger, and handling_fee_outstanding is 0.00 on both
  agreements.

PERSONA DESIGN
Baxter Sudbury is written as a school business manager: formal, patient, reading off a printout, with the seasonal weariness
of somebody who does the IT refresh twice a year. He volunteers the goal (the first wave collected on the first of October),
the registered name, the hard preference on the day, and the one boundary he cares about — releasing the machines is the
school's decision, because the laptops are school property and the drives carry pupil work. Everything else is on request:
the mobile and the card's last four, the postal code, the forty six machines on the schedule, the three laptops going back
from the August delivery, the balance on the fleet line, the ShieldCare cover. His reactions are tied to what the agent
says: if the wave comes back smaller he accepts it and asks only that the day is kept; if the agent puts a lower offer to
him he asks what the figure is and says to put it through; if the agent tells him the money has been credited he asks for it
against the invoice account rather than a transfer; when the release is handed to him he runs it and reads the count and the
date back. He never mentions the older batch first, never names a figure gold writes, and if the agent never raises the
batch he says nothing about it. His last reaction answers the wave going on record, which is the last gold action, and he
asks for nothing beyond it.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION, UNDER ONE FROZEN CLOCK
He gives the registered name -> find_customers; the mobile and the card's last four -> verify_customer_identity; the agent
reads both agreements, the batch's trade-in history, both shipment requests, the ShieldCare plan, the return
authorisations and their events, the orders and the fleet line; asks how many machines are on the schedule (forty six),
whether anything else is going back (three laptops, collection arranged), about the account (a balance on the fleet line)
and about the cover (yes, premium still being taken) — all answered in the persona, including the answers that never enter
a gold argument; the agent explains the appraisal came back lower and puts the revised offer, he accepts it in the call,
which is what the programme's decision days allow him to do at once; the agent credits the batch and asks how he wants it,
he says the invoice account; the agent works out the wave, unlocks the release, hands it over, and he runs it; the agent
confirms the wave is on record and he closes. Nothing waits on a delivery, a payment clearing, an approval, a batch job or
a future date: the collection on 2026-10-01 is booked, not performed, and no write in the tree depends on it.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT
  Crediting the batch on the 5100.00 the appraisal supports: the credit policy's own rule says the amount credited is
  worked out only after the revised offer stands on the history, and the settled figure is then the revised offer.
  Measuring the gap against the appraisal rather than the figure the agreement stands at, or forgetting that the tolerance
  is a percentage of that figure rather than a flat sum.
  Taking the whole revised offer for 18 devices when 21 were declared: the share rule is explicit, and the three devices
  short are settled separately under the transit cover rather than through the offer.
  Counting the inspection of 2025-05-20 inside the twelve months, which would make the wave 7 machines.
  Reading the placed order of 2026-09-14 as a recent purchase, which would hold back 4 machines instead of 2.
  Paying the credit without the erasure holdback, the premium holdback or the interim credit, each of which the rule states.
  Releasing the 46 machines the caller has crated, or the 12 the cover bears, instead of the 5 the rule leaves.
  Booking the wave before the batch stands credited: the wave policy's own rule forbids it, and the eligibility it waits on
  would not hold.

THE STANDARD SOLUTION
Verify the profile. Read both agreements; see the buyback batch standing appraised at 5100.00 against 6300.00 quoted with no
revision on its history, and the refresh schedule standing quoted for 46 machines at 9200.00. Put the revised offer: the gap
of 1200.00 sits between the 630.00 tolerance and twice it, so start at 5700.00; take 18 of the 21 declared; the batch was
booked in 15 days after a 14-day quote, so the ageing runs from the quote day, 29 days, above 21, so 12 percent comes off:
4299.43. Credit the batch: 4299.43 settled, less the 900.00 interim credit, plus 900.00 of transit settlement on three
devices at 300.00, plus the 60.00 delayed-appraisal allowance, less the 240.00 premium outstanding, less 300.00 for twelve
uncertified machines: 3819.43, as invoice credit. Then the wave: the cover bears 12 machines, less 3 for the live return,
2 for the order fulfilled on the fifth and 2 for the fleet line balance: 5 machines, released by the caller for 2026-10-01.

RULE / COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses carries a verbatim quotation in its policy's compute_basis (checked
mechanically: every compute_basis value is a whitespace-normalised substring of its own rule). Backward: the windows

Baxter Sudbury is the business manager at Oakhurst Ridge Academy, a two hundred pupil independent school on the east side of Portland, and the IT refresh is his headache twice a year. He is patient on the phone and a little formal, the sort of caller who reads the reference off a printout and waits to be told what happens next. What he rings about is the new refresh schedule Northbeam quoted him a couple of days ago for the classroom laptops: the crates are being made up in the old library and he wants the first wave collected on the first of October, which is the day the hall is free and the caretaker is in. He says at the start that Northbeam should arrange the freight, but that releasing the machines is the school's decision and he will confirm that part himself, because the laptops are school property and the drives carry pupil work.

He gives the school's registered name, Oakhurst Ridge Academy, and if he is asked to prove who he is he reads out the school office mobile, 5037740193, and the last four of the card the school keeps on file, 4106. He can give the postal code 97251 as a third detail. He has no internal reference numbers and says so: the paperwork on his desk is a purchase order printout, nothing more.

Asked how many machines are in the refresh, he says forty six are on the schedule and the crates will hold them all. If the agent comes back and says the first wave can only take a smaller number, he accepts it without pushing, says the rest can go on the next wave, and asks only that the first of October is kept. He will not move that day. Asked whether anything else is going back to Northbeam he mentions, only if asked, that five of the new laptops from the August delivery are going back because the department over-ordered and a collection has been arranged for those. Asked about the school's account he says the academy buys everything on the fleet line and there is a balance on it at the moment, the October invoice. Asked about the cover on the older laptops he says yes, there is a ShieldCare fleet policy and he thinks the monthly premium is still being taken.

He knows nothing about what has happened to the batch of older Latitudes the school sent in at the start of September beyond the fact that they went. If the agent tells him the appraisal came back below what was quoted and puts a lower offer to him, he listens, asks what the figure is, and then says that is disappointing but acceptable and to put it through; he is not going to argue over a pallet of five year old laptops. If the agent asks how the school wants anything owing on that batch paid, he says to put it against the academy's invoice account rather than a transfer, because that is how everything else goes through the school's books, and he says the same if he is told afterwards that the money has been credited.
